newsitem.title: CHINA: New listings to help develop China's B markets.
newsitem.headline: New listings to help develop China's B markets.

text.p: China's selection of 33 firms for B share listings shows the government's determination to develop the B share markets and will make them more active and open, the China Securities newspaper said on Friday.
The securities authorities on Tuesday unveiled a list of 33 companies to be considered for foreign currency B share listings on the domestic stock markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen.

The newspaper said it was the first time the national securities authorities had selected candidates for B share listings as they have done hitherto only for companies to be listed on overseas stock markets.
Last month, the authorities also named 38 companies for listing abroad, most of which are expected to be listed as H shares in Hong Kong.

"It shows the government's determination and confidence in continuing to develop the B share market," the newspaper quoted Jiang Dengfu, an analyst with the Shenyin-Wanguo Securities, as saying. "It will make the B share market more open."

The new listings, with an average capitalisation of $50 million, will significantly enlarge the markets and help to attract more foreign investors, the newspaper quoted Hoong Yik Luen of ING-Barings in Shanghai as saying.
The currently-listed B share companies are mostly small with average capitalisation of $20-30 million, which are more susceptible to economic fluctuations, Hoong said.
